CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine yearly exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Christine is a 63-year-old female presenting for her annual physical examination. She reports feeling well overall. Regarding her depression, she is doing great with good symptom management. She is taking her prescribed antidepressant medication and attending therapy weekly, which has been helpful. She is sleeping well, getting a full eight hours of sleep per night, and denies any suicidal ideation. 

Regarding her hypertension, she has been checking her blood pressure at home and reports it has been fluctuating, with readings either elevated or low over the past couple of weeks without staying stable despite taking her blood pressure medication regularly. She reports her diet has been inconsistent lately due to work-related stress and increased work hours, resulting in consumption of more frozen meals and less time for grocery shopping and meal preparation. She reports some headaches, which she attributes to prolonged computer screen exposure at work.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No numbness or tingling in hands or fingers. No abnormal swelling. Otherwise, review of systems is negative.

2. Depression: Patient is doing well on current regimen with good adherence to medication and therapy. No changes made at this time. Continue current antidepressant medication and weekly therapy.

3. Carpal tunnel syndrome: Status post right wrist release two years ago with good ongoing results. No current symptoms. Patient instructed to report any recurrence of tingling or other symptoms.
